questions.question: Does this DPO loop require a separately trained reward model and fresh policy rollouts?
options: No. It optimizes reference-corrected preferences from the supplied pairs.
No, and a positive reference-corrected margin guarantees that the absolute chosen probability increased.
Yes, because the reference log-probability difference must be re-estimated from on-policy rollouts each step.
questions.explanation: DPO uses offline preference pairs and a fixed reference policy rather than an online reward-model rollout loop. Its reference-corrected relative objective does not guarantee higher absolute chosen probability or better independently evaluated outputs.
optionFeedback: DPO uses offline preference pairs and a fixed reference policy rather than an online reward-model rollout loop. Its reference-corrected relative objective does not guarantee higher absolute chosen probability or better independently evaluated outputs.
A relative chosen-versus-rejected margin can improve while both absolute probabilities fall. Compare both log probabilities and their difference.
The reference is a fixed policy in this offline objective. It is not an on-policy estimate updated from rollouts.
